part.text: I'll scaffold a TypeScript static site generator CLI with the required features: frontmatter parsing, Handlebars layouts and partials, tag index pages, RSS generation, a dev server with live reload, and syntax highlighting. I'll also add package.json, tsconfig.json, and comprehensive Vitest tests. Proceeding to add the project files and implementation.

part.text:
I implemented a TypeScript static site generator CLI with all requested features, tests, and configuration.

What’s included
- Core
  - Frontmatter parsing: title, date, tags, draft (via gray-matter)
  - Markdown rendering with syntax highlighting (markdown-it + highlight.js)
  - Handlebars templates:
    - Layouts: templates/layouts/*.hbs
    - Partials: templates/partials/**/*.hbs (auto-registered by relative path)
    - Optional page templates: templates/pages/*.hbs selected via frontmatter template
  - Tag index pages: generated at output/tags/<tag>/index.html
  - RSS feed: rss.xml at the output root (requires --site-title and --site-url)
  - Dev server with live reload: chokidar watch, ws WebSocket reload, HTML injection
- CLI
  - Commands: build (default) and serve
  - Flags:
    - -s, --src <dir>
    - -t, --templates <dir>
    - -o, --out <dir>
    - --include-drafts
    - --site-title <title>
    - --site-url <url>
    - --base-url <base>
    - serve only: -p, --port <port> (default 5173)
- Tests (Vitest)
  - Frontmatter parsing and draft filtering
  - Template rendering with partials/layout and syntax highlighting
  - Tag index and RSS generation
  - Dev server live reload injection
  - CLI flag behavior (--include-drafts) with a compiled CLI invocation
- Project config
  - package.json with bin: ssg and scripts for build/test
  - tsconfig.json targeting Node CJS, outDir dist
  - Test fixtures with a minimal site and templates

Key files
- src/cli.ts: CLI entry (ssg)
- src/build.ts: buildSite core
- src/server.ts: serveWithLiveReload dev server
- src/templates.ts: load layouts/partials/pages and render helpers
- src/markdown.ts: markdown-it + highlight.js setup
- src/rss.ts: RSS feed generation
- src/types.ts, src/utils.ts: shared types/helpers
- tests/ssg.test.ts: comprehensive tests
- tests/fixtures/site: example content and templates used by tests

Usage
- Build:
  - npx ts-node not required; compile then run:
    - npm run build
    - node dist/cli.js build -s ./content -t ./templates -o ./public --site-title "My Site" --site-url https://example.com
  - Or use the default command (build) without subcommand:
    - node dist/cli.js -s ./content -t ./templates -o ./public
- Serve with live reload:
  - node dist/cli.js serve -s ./content -t ./templates -o ./public -p 5173 --site-title "My Site" --site-url https://example.com
- Tests:
  - npm test
  - Test script builds first, then runs Vitest (includes a CLI behavior test via the compiled dist/cli.js)

Template conventions
- Layouts: templates/layouts/main.hbs is the default; you can select a different layout per page with frontmatter layout.
- Partials: any templates/partials/**/*.hbs are auto-registered by their relative path without extension (e.g., partials/header.hbs => {{> header}}).
- Page template: Optional frontmatter template resolves against templates/pages/*.hbs; if present, the rendered result is inserted into the chosen layout’s {{{body}}}.
- Context available to templates:
  - site: { title, url, baseUrl }
  - page: frontmatter + normalized fields
  - content: rendered Markdown HTML
  - allPages: non-draft pages sorted by date desc
  - tags: array of { tag, count }
  - urlPath: output-relative URL path to the page

Notes
- Drafts are excluded by default; include them with --include-drafts.
- Tag pages default to a built-in simple listing if templates/tag.hbs is not provided.
- RSS generation requires both --site-title and --site-url to be set.
- Live reload script is injected automatically by the dev server; rebuilds and broadcasts occur on changes in src or templates.

If you want me to add a README, expand CLI options, or support copying static assets (images, CSS) alongside HTML, say the word and I’ll add it.
